title: Glasshouse — institutional accountability evidence dataset (say vs. do)
description:
Glasshouse is a public, machine-readable record of what large asset managers say about how they vote their funds' shares (archived proxy-voting and stewardship policies, with dates) and how those funds actually voted (SEC Form N-PX), with 13-F holdings and a public enforcement record alongside.

This version holds 23,395,801 fund vote lines from SEC Form N-PX filings for the voting years July 2023 to June 2026, filed by fund trusts of 35 financial institutions. For 32 of them (BlackRock, Dimensional, Vanguard, State Street, Fidelity, American Century, Nuveen/TIAA, PGIM, Thrivent, Victory Capital, Principal, Capital Group, Columbia Threadneedle, Northern Trust, MFS, Morgan Stanley, Franklin Templeton including Putnam, AllianceBernstein, Wellington, Federated Hermes, Goldman Sachs, Allspring, J.P. Morgan, Parametric, Janus Henderson, Neuberger Berman, Invesco, Lord Abbett, Charles Schwab, DWS, T. Rowe Price, BNY) every kind of vote is on file for the fund trusts held; for UBS, BNP Paribas and Bank of America only executive-pay (say-on-pay) votes are on file. The fund trusts held are often a small part of a large manager: this is not a complete record of any manager's voting. Some 2025–2026 Dimensional N-PX exhibits contain exactly 500,000 proxy records in the SEC file itself and appear capped, so their counts are lower bounds. It also holds 248 dated versions of 33 managers' policy documents (hashes, dates and archive links; no policy text), 580,106 13-F holding rows and 14,887 enforcement actions.

Correction. Versions 2026-11-17.2, 2026-11-17.3, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-18.2 shipped repeated N-PX vote lines as distinct votes (0.62–0.69% of their votes; mostly Dimensional, whose line counts there are about 3% too high). This version is corrected: no shipped vote is a marked duplicate, and the build now refuses to run when duplicate flags are stale. Per-release counts: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not/blob/main/docs/CORRECTIONS.md

New in this version: Principal, PGIM, Victory Capital and Thrivent fund registrants (about 2.7 million vote lines), each keyed to its voting adviser from the funds' own SAIs and Form N-CEN, with dated policy text. PGIM's funds are keyed per series to the subadviser that votes them (Jennison, PGIM Quantitative Solutions, PGIM, Inc. or an external subadviser); the former Pioneer funds now run by Victory are keyed AMUNDI_US until 31 March 2025, so their earlier votes are not compared with Victory's policy. A policy version's identity now also ignores soft hyphens and words hyphenated across a line break, and a policy printed in a fund SAI is read only from SAIs of the same family, so page layout differences no longer appear as new versions. Meeting dates written with a two-digit year (one 2024 Wellington filing) are now read correctly.

Votes are attributed to the adviser that cast them, not the brand: where one group's funds are voted by different advisers under different policies every vote carries an adviser_key, and a policy may only be compared with votes of the same key. Three derived tables give one row per manager per ballot item (shareholder proposals, director elections, say-on-pay). Every column and code is defined in DATASHEET.md; coverage and known gaps are stated in COVERAGE.json; every file is checksummed in MANIFEST.sha256.

Code: https://github.com/glasshouse-records/promises-kept-or-not (MIT). The DATASHEET records the exact code commit that built these files.

The dataset records facts from public filings. It makes no finding of wrongdoing about anyone.
notes: Code: MIT. Data: CC-BY-4.0. Built from code commit recorded in DATASHEET.md.
